transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-04 16:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Amy Chen (Redwood AE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (HelmTech CTO), Jon Berg (HelmTech SRE), Evan Cho (HelmTech PM)

Summary (auto): Quick console tour focusing on request tracing and graceful fallback. AE opened, SE demoed. Heavy discussion on KV-cache behavior under bursty traffic and how console surfaces fallbacks and correlates logs to traces.

[00:00] Amy Chen: alright everyone thanks for joining, uh this is Amy from Redwood. we have Luis our solutions engineer with me. how's it going?
[00:14] Maya Patel: doing good, thanks. we just stepped out of another internal sync so apologies if we're a few minutes late, we have Jon and Evan on too.
[00:20] Jon Berg: hey all.
[00:23] Luis Ortega: good to meet you all. quick agenda — we'll do a 30 minute console walk-through, show trace -> request log stitching, then talk about fallback policies and private deployment considerations, leave time for q&a. sound ok?
[00:36] Evan Cho: yep that works.
[00:40] Amy Chen: and just to call out, give us any examples of where you saw odd latency or unexpected model costs so we can focus on that. Maya you mentioned KV cache misses earlier in email?
[00:52] Maya Patel: yes, we saw... like spikes where latency doubled and token cost spiked. it seemed to line up with certain user journeys — chat to summary conversion — and we want to understand if Redwood can keep those steady.
[01:06] Luis Ortega: perfect, we'll pull that thread. I'll share a demo trace first.

--- Demo start ---
[01:15] Luis Ortega: ok sharing screen — this is the console trace inspector. top-left, you can search by correlation id, user id, or route. i pasted a sample trace id from our synthetic run, you'll see the waterfall with service calls, then the inference node, expand that.
[01:30] Speaker 2: hmm that pane doesn't look familiar — is that the new layout?
[01:35] Luis Ortega: yeah, we released a small nav tweak in July, sometimes ff will show the older label, ignore that.
[01:42] Luis Ortega: expanding inference span — you'll see metadata: model variant, quantization profile, batch size, and the KV-cache hit rate. here the cache shows 84% hit and there's a 120ms queued wait attributable to batching overhead.
[02:00] Jon Berg: when cache drops to 0 what's the fallback? do you immediately call a larger model or smell — sorry 'smell' is my microphone — do you throttle?
[02:12] Luis Ortega: good question. so fallback is policy driven. you can set per-route: try kv-cache -> cheap quantized variant -> full accuracy variant. we also have a <graceful-degrade> policy where, under high queue latency, it will route to a smaller variant to keep p95 under the SLO.
[02:30] Amy Chen: and that routing is visible in the trace — you'll see automatic variant selection events and the console annotates why the fallback happened (e.g., cache miss, queue saturation, model OOM).
[02:42] Maya Patel: can you show an example where fallback increased correctness regressions? we can't sacrifice critical accuracy in billing flows.
[02:51] Luis Ortega: sure — switching to a trace where we forced a fallback — here the model variant label flips and there's an 'eval score' event showing a quick BLEU-ish metric we compute against a golden set for that job. you'll see a modest drop from 0.91 to 0.87. we flag that in the quality monitor and surface a regression alert.
[03:14] Evan Cho: is that golden set something we upload? how do you handle PII?
[03:20] Luis Ortega: yes you can upload scrubbed prompt-output pairs into Redwood Optimize evals. for PII we recommend local anonymization or using Redwood Private so data doesn't leave your VPC — or you can use our hosted redaction pipeline.
[03:33] Jon Berg: on Private, two questions: audit logs — do we get raw request logs and audit trails to send to our SIEM? and kms integration?
[03:42] Amy Chen: yep — for Private we ship raw request/response logs to your S3 or on-prem storage, plus structured audit events. KMS/HSM integrations are supported, and we'll include those details in the security pack.
[03:54] Maya Patel: what's the retention on hosted? we can't keep raw transcripts longer than 30 days for compliance.
[04:00] Amy Chen: hosted default is 90 days but we can configure retention down to 30 for enterprise customers, and Private you control retention entirely.
[04:10] Speaker 1: nice

[04:15] Luis Ortega: back to traces — another neat part is request-log stitching. click the request ID in the trace and it opens the raw request payload, headers, and a small token cost breakdown. here you can also replay a request in the sandbox to reproduce behavior (replay mode preserves the original routing rules).
[04:38] Maya Patel: how deterministic is replay with cached prefixes or KV state?
[04:44] Luis Ortega: great point. replay can simulate the original request but cache state is captured as a snapshot in the trace metadata — if a replay depends on a warmed prefix it will note a cache-miss and we provide a 'warm cache' toggle to seed the KV snapshot for more faithful replays.
[05:04] Jon Berg: and for rolling back an upgrade, can we use the console to route a portion of traffic to the old variant?
[05:11] Luis Ortega: yes — rollout controls let you do canary percentages per route. the console also surfaces comparative traces for both variants so you can inspect regressions side-by-side.

[05:28] Amy Chen: quick pause — Evan, what's the internal decision timeline? do you need legal and security sign-offs before POC?
[05:36] Evan Cho: we'll need security review for sure, legal maybe later for contract terms. we'd like to have a POC scoped in two weeks if possible.
[05:44] Amy Chen: good — we'll prioritize the security pack and the KV fallback diagram.

[05:52] Luis Ortega: moving on — fault injection and error analysis. console shows errors by class: OOM, model timeout, network, and we'll surface root-cause traces. here's a trace with a transient model OOM; the console has a helper 'suggested mitigations' panel that recommends smaller batch, switch quant profile, or a config to auto-failover to a CPU-bound variant.
[06:18] Maya Patel: is the suggested mitigations panel configurable? we have internal rules that forbid dropping below X accuracy for billing flows.
[06:25] Luis Ortega: yep you can override recommendations and pin routes to disallow specific fallbacks. we'll show RBAC controls later.

[06:34] Jon Berg: latency budgets — can the console alert on token-level latency anomalies? we need to know if certain prompts spike tail latencies.
[06:42] Luis Ortega: yes, token-level histograms are available per-route and you can create alerting rules (p95 token time > 80ms) that integrate with PagerDuty/Slack.

[06:55] Evan Cho: curious about cost reporting — we saw a spike last month and want to tie billing to product feature. can we tag requests?
[07:02] Amy Chen: yes, there's request-level metadata tags; you can attach feature flags or team IDs and then the Console Cost Explorer lets you roll up costs by tag.

[07:12] Speaker 3: (inaudible)

[07:20] Luis Ortega: next i want to demo an error triage flow. starting from an alert, you click the trace and the console highlights the first failed span. you'll see correlated logs from upstream services and the inference node. for example here you'll see a downstream microservice returned 502 causing request replays to pile up, which in turn overloaded the inference pool and triggered fallbacks.
[07:45] Maya Patel: so the console stitches across our services as long as we pass the correlation id?
[07:50] Luis Ortega: exactly — we support tracing headers X-Request-ID, X-Correlation-ID and OpenTelemetry context. if you emit those, Console will stitch.

[08:02] Jon Berg: any sample code to instrument our workload?
[08:05] Luis Ortega: yes — we have SDK snippets for Node/Python/Go in the docs; i'll include them in the follow-up.

[08:12] Amy Chen: pivot a bit — Maya you mentioned regional constraints?
[08:16] Maya Patel: right, we have EU customers; we'd prefer inference to run in eu-west-1 and logs to stay in eu-s3. hosted multi-region is ok as long as data residency rules are followed.
[08:27] Amy Chen: we support region pinning per-account and per-route. for stricter needs, Redwood Private can be deployed in your VPC in eu-west-1.

[08:36] Evan Cho: what about high availability — do you shard requests across AZs?
[08:40] Luis Ortega: yes, the serving runtime has AZ-aware placement and autoscaling policies; the console shows replication and failure domains. if an AZ goes down, requests are routed to other AZs with a brief failover window — the trace will show a route migration event.

[08:58] Speaker 4: um

[09:02] Luis Ortega: ok i want to show a short search session for a noisy customer journey. searching by user id shows a series of traces; we can overlay p95 latency and token cost across the timeline to find when costs spiked — here a new prompt template caused the model to produce longer outputs, token cost spiked. you can pin that trace and create a 'checklist' action right from the console for devs to triage.
[09:29] Jon Berg: can you export those traces in a zipped json for offline analysis?
[09:34] Luis Ortega: yes, export to NDJSON or open telemetry format. you can also push to your S3/ELK.

[09:44] Maya Patel: one more on fallback: if a request is partially served by cache and partially misses, how is that represented?
[09:50] Luis Ortega: the trace splits the inference span into sub-spans: 'cache check', 'prefix fetch', 'model generation'. you'll see annotations for each token range indicating which source served it. we also compute a blended cost metric for that request.

[10:06] Amy Chen: switching to security briefly: for hosted we'd provide SOC2 documentation, pen test summary, SSO SAML integration, and audit log export. Private adds KMS integrations and no egress. Luis will drop that pack in email.

[10:23] Evan Cho: fine — what does the pilot look like? would it be a dedicated pool for us?
[10:28] Amy Chen: pilots are flexible — could be a small Dedicated pool with reserved capacity for predictable latency, or a Private trial in your VPC for compliance testing. usually 4 weeks to validate SLOs and integration.

[10:40] Maya Patel: how much engineering effort to run the SDK and trace headers?
[10:45] Luis Ortega: minimal — a couple of instrumentation points to propagate correlation ids and to tag requests. we can help with a runbook during POC.

[10:52] Jon Berg: curious about autoscaling — can we set hard concurrency limits per-customer? we rate limit on our side and need graceful backpressure to avoid cascade failures.
[11:02] Luis Ortega: yes per-route concurrency and burst policies exist, and you can opt into queue priority classes. the runtime will return structured error codes for throttling so upstream can handle backoff.

[11:17] Amy Chen: quick check — any blockers on compliance?
[11:20] Maya Patel: main blocker is KMS + audit chain. once we have specifics we'll escalate.

[11:26] Luis Ortega: switching to forensic replay — here's the replay UI. you pick a trace, enable 'seed kv snapshot' if you want cache-warm behavior, and run in a sandbox that uses the same routing rules. it'll show a side-by-side of original vs replay timings.
[11:45] Evan Cho: can replay runs hit production models?
[11:49] Luis Ortega: sandbox replay is isolated but you can configure a staging pool that uses production-like images. we don't recommend hitting production models without isolation.

[11:58] Speaker 2: hmm

[12:05] Luis Ortega: last demo piece — alerts and incident handoff. we have a 'create incident' workflow that attaches traces, suggested mitigations, relevant runbook links, and can push to your ticketing system. this reduces time-to-triage.
[12:20] Jon Berg: that integration with our internal pager is critical.
[12:23] Amy Chen: we'll include endpoints and auth patterns for PagerDuty in the security pack.

[12:30] Maya Patel: ok this has been helpful. quick question — how are you charging for request replays and trace exports?
[12:36] Amy Chen: small metered fee for replays and exports on hosted, included in Dedicated reserved capacity plans up to X ops, we'll put exact numbers in the pilot pricing doc.

[12:48] Evan Cho: any competitor pitfalls we should be aware of?
[12:51] Amy Chen: some vendors don't capture KV-state with traces which makes replay fidelity poor; others require you to wire a separate tracing system. Redwood tries to be a single pane: traces, logs, and request payloads with replay fidelity.

[13:05] Speaker 1: mm-hmm

[13:10] Luis Ortega: ok wrapping towards Q&A.
[13:12] Maya Patel: can you demo a noisy trace export? we'd like to see a sample to share with our infra team.
[13:18] Luis Ortega: i already pulled one from our sandbox — i'll attach it to the follow-up email and include instructions on how to interpret the spans.

[13:28] Jon Berg: one last: do you surface KV eviction events? We saw some evictions that correlated with misses.
[13:34] Luis Ortega: yes eviction events are recorded as trace annotations and you can set alerts on eviction rate.

[13:42] Amy Chen: great. i'll recap next steps at the end. any final questions?
[13:48] Evan Cho: what SLA levels do you offer for Dedicated?
[13:52] Amy Chen: Dedicated has an SLA with 99.9% uptime and latency SLO guard rails — exact numbers depend on the commitment level, we'll include that in pilot pricing.

[14:05] Maya Patel: thanks, this is helpful.
[14:08] Luis Ortega: cool — to close, we'll email the security pack, KV fallback diagram, the exported trace and a proposed POC plan.
[14:16] Amy Chen: perfect. thanks everyone, we'll follow up.

--- End of recording (14:20) ---

Notes: transcript has occasional mis-attributions and filler. The recorded demo run nested multiple console flows; recommended follow-ups are security docs, exported traces, and a POC scoping call.
